text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwanese buyers will probably tender for up to 100,000 tonnes of soybeans and 8,000 tonnes of corn next week, traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka seeks 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of PL-480 wheat for June 30-July 19 shipment. Offers are due by 1630 GMT June 5 at the Sri Lanka embassy in Washington.
BARLEY TENDER - Iran on June 9 will seek 100,000 tonnes of optional feed barley for September shipment, European traders said.

CORN TENDER - Naseem Agriculture of Abu Dhabi seeks 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine or South African yellow maize for second half August shipment, South Africa's shippers association said. Bids are due June 6.

RICE TENDER - Pakistan's Rice Export Corporation should decide in the next two days on three bids for the export of 5,000 tonnes of basmati variety Pak-7 1996/97 (July-June) rice, containing seven percent broken, an official said.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs seeks offers June 4 to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for July with confirmation on June 12.

VEGOIL AND TALLOW TENDERS - El Salvador seeks 4,500 tonnes prime bleachable summer yellow cottonseed oil in bulk and about 1,000 tonnes of sunflowerseed oil under the PL-480 export program for July 20-August 5 shipment. Offers are to be received no later than June 16 and remain valid June 17. El Salvador also seeks on June 16 about 1,650 tonnes of tallow and approximately 800 tonnes of top white tallow. Shipment dates for both lots of tallow were set for July 20-August 5.

MARKET TALK - Thailand said on Friday its rice exports from January to early June dropped by more than 25 percent from the same period last year due to weaker global demand and lower-than-expected supplies in the country.

... A U.S. agricultural attache said U.S. wheat sales to Colombia may suffer because recent economic measures by the Colombian government have eliminated the attractiveness for Colombian bankers and importers to use the U.S. Agriculture Department's GSM-102 program.

... Philippine hog farmers are expected to shop for more corn in the coming week to meet short term requirements, Manila grains traders said. Traders said they have received inquiries for imports of 25,000 tonnes yellow corn.
